historical_references.reference: Isander of Andros was a Christian martyr who lived during the Diocletian Persecution in the late 3rd century AD. He was born on the island of Andros, and was a deacon in the local church. Isander was arrested and brought before the Roman governor, who asked him to offer sacrifices to the gods. Isander refused and was tortured and imprisoned. He was eventually brought before Diocletian himself, who ordered him to be executed. Isander was beheaded, becoming a revered martyr in the Christian tradition.

Isander of Gaul was a Christian bishop who lived in the 5th century AD. He is best known for his role in the Council of Arles in 450 AD, where he attempted to reconcile the differences between the Celtic and Roman forms of Christianity in the region. Isander's efforts were ultimately unsuccessful, as the two groups remained distinct for centuries to come. Isander continued to serve as bishop of his see in Gaul until his death.
